title: Adverse Drug Reactions: Type A and Type B Patterns
subject: Pharmacology
preview: Type A adverse drug reactions are predictable from known pharmacology and often dose-related.
quickRevision: Type A adverse drug reactions are predictable from known pharmacology and often dose-related.
Examples of Type A patterns include anticoagulant-related bleeding; severe hypersensitivity illustrates an important Type B pattern.
Detailed timing, concomitant medication and dechallenge information help assess causality.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Type A adverse drug reactions are predictable from known pharmacology and often dose-related.
Type B reactions are usually less predictable and not simply explained by the usual dose-dependent mechanism.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Examples of Type A patterns include anticoagulant-related bleeding; severe hypersensitivity illustrates an important Type B pattern.
Detailed timing, concomitant medication and dechallenge information help assess causality.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not label every adverse event as an allergy; mechanism matters for future prescribing.

quiz.question: Which ADR class is commonly dose-related and pharmacologically predictable?
quiz.explanation: Type A adverse drug reactions are predictable from known pharmacology and often dose-related.
